title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
description:
A subsequence keeps the original order of elements but may skip some. Find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of an array.

Input format
Line 1: n.
Line 2: n integers.

Output format
One integer: the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000. Values fit in a 32-bit signed integer.
hints: Let best[i] be the length of the longest increasing subsequence that ends at index i. How can best[i] be computed from earlier values?
best[i] = 1 + max(best[j]) over j < i with a[j] < a[i]. That is O(n^2) and enough for small inputs.

For large n keep a list "tails" where tails[L] is the smallest possible last value of an increasing subsequence of length L+1. For each value, binary-search the first tail >= value (bisect_left) and replace it, or append if none. Use bisect_left for strictly increasing sequences.

examples.explanation: Equal values are not strictly increasing, so the best length is 1.
